# Kyoto School quotes

The Kyoto School brings Zen and Mahayana insights into dialogue with Western philosophy, especially around nothingness, experience, and the religious worldview.

16 passages · 3 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Nishida’s logic of place and contradictory self-identity, Nishitani’s religion and nothingness, and related figures (including Watsuji’s ethics of betweenness in adjacent debates) shape this hub’s English passages.

## Historical notes

Emerging around Kyoto University in the early twentieth century, the school remains central to comparative philosophy of religion and modern Japanese thought.

## Core ideas

-   Absolute nothingness is not mere negation.
-   Self and world co-determine in the place (basho) of experience.
-   Religion discloses a logic ordinary objectivity misses.
-   Emptiness (śūnyatā) can be philosophically articulated without slogans.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Nishida Kitaro](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/nishida-kitaro) , [Nishitani Keiji](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/nishitani-keiji) , [Watsuji Tetsuro](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/watsuji-tetsuro)

## FAQ

### What is the Kyoto School?

It is a modern Japanese philosophical movement engaging Western philosophy with Mahayana and Zen concepts, especially nothingness and experience.

### Who are major Kyoto School thinkers?

Nishida Kitaro and Nishitani Keiji are central; related figures appear alongside them in comparative ethics and religion.

### Where can I find Kyoto School quotes?

This school page gathers verified English renderings from the archive’s Kyoto School label.
